Desktop current-main codebase_telemetry is a Sand/Linux-only telemetry extension: it snapshots the Sand /workspace + /home codebases through an external csnaps process, applies privacy/auth lifecycle and uploads codebase telemetry around agent request start/end.

The Desktop local mechanism cannot exist in the Android app because Android has neither authority over the Sand filesystem nor permission to spawn the arbitrary csnaps process. Treating phone storage as the codebase would change the product meaning and violate scoped-storage/privacy boundaries.

Replacement: the actual Sand/Desktop execution environment remains the owner of its own codebase telemetry. Android does not create a hidden codebase-telemetry Remote Runner executor and does not expose this privilege through WebView/UI. Existing authorized Remote Runner remains for explicit user capabilities only.

tests/test_codebase_telemetry_android_replacement.py enforces no local codebase_telemetry module, no csnaps string in Android Host/local runner, and no hidden codebase-telemetry/csnaps Remote tool while retaining account-fenced approved Remote Runner primitives. Exact-head Actions evidence remains required before verification.
